Found under Settings, Health checks.

<a id="page-health"></a>

## About this page

Chooses what the Health page shows: its score, and which kinds of problem it lists.

#### How it works

These switches change only what is shown. The checks themselves run on this device and send nothing anywhere. The one exception is a breach check you start yourself, on [Breaches](/guide/settings/breaches/).

**Page** has the score. **Problems to list** has one switch for each kind of problem.

See also [Health screen](/guide/screens/#screen-health), [Password health](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-health), [Breaches](/guide/settings/breaches/).

<a id="setting-health-score"></a>

## Show the score

Shows a score out of 100 at the top of the Health page.

#### How it works

The score is the share of your logins whose password has none of these problems: easy to guess, used more than once, in a known breach, or not changed in a year.

Logins without a password are not counted, and nor is anything in the trash. A vault with no logins scores 100.

#### Limits

Turning checks off under [Problems to list](/guide/settings/health/#group-health-problems) hides them from the page but does not change the score. The other checks, such as unencrypted sites, never change it.

See also [Problems to list](/guide/settings/health/#group-health-problems), [Health screen](/guide/screens/#screen-health).

<a id="setting-health-skip-local"></a>

## Leave out local addresses

Leaves logins for devices on your own network out of the Health checks: a router, a NAS, a printer.

#### Why it is there

These sit behind your router, out of reach of the leaks and guessing the checks warn about, and many cannot use https or a second factor at all.

#### How it works

A login counts as local when every address saved on it is a private or loopback IP, or a name with no dot or one ending in .local, .lan, .home, .internal or .localhost.

See also [Problems to list](/guide/settings/health/#group-health-problems), [Health screen](/guide/screens/#screen-health).

<a id="group-health-problems"></a>

## Problems to list

Each switch shows or hides one kind of problem on the Health page.

#### How it works

A hidden check still runs. Its items are left off the page, and the score is worked out the same way.

#### When to use it

Hide a kind of problem you have decided to live with, such as old passwords for sites that hold nothing you care about.

See also [Show the score](/guide/settings/health/#setting-health-score), [Health screen](/guide/screens/#screen-health).

<a id="action-health-check-breached"></a>

## In a known breach

Lists logins whose password has turned up in a published leak. When there are any, they come first on the Health page.

#### How it works

This list fills only after you run [Check every password](/guide/settings/breaches/#action-check-every-password) on the Breaches page. The results are never saved, so it empties when the vault locks.

#### Limits

The browser extension cannot run that check, so there this list stays empty.

See also [Check every password](/guide/settings/breaches/#action-check-every-password), [Breaches](/guide/settings/breaches/).

<a id="action-health-check-reused"></a>

## Used more than once

Lists logins that share a password with at least one other login.

#### Why it is there

When one site leaks a password, attackers try it on other sites. A different password for each login keeps a leak to one site.

See also [Generator](/guide/settings/generator/), [Duplicate items](/guide/settings/health/#action-health-check-duplicates).

<a id="action-health-check-weak"></a>

## Easy to guess

Lists logins whose password would fall quickly to an attacker working through likely passwords.

#### How it works

WM Pass rates each password on this device. Words from the site's name, the username and the item's title count as easy guesses, so a password built from them rates lower.

See also [Generator](/guide/settings/generator/), [Compare two passwords](/guide/settings/compare/).

<a id="action-health-check-insecure"></a>

## Unencrypted sites

Lists logins saved with a web address that starts with http:// rather than https://.

#### Why it is there

On a plain http page, a password can be read on its way to the site. If the site offers https, change the saved address.

<a id="action-health-check-expiring"></a>

## Expiring soon

Lists items whose expiry date is close or has already passed.

<a id="action-health-check-old"></a>

## Not changed in a year

Lists logins whose password has not changed for a year, or for longer than the item's own reminder.

#### How it works

An item with a reminder set under **Remind me to change it** is measured against that reminder instead of a year.

#### Limits

The age counts from when the password last changed in WM Pass, so imported passwords start again from the day of the import.

<a id="action-health-check-twofactor"></a>

## No second factor

Lists logins for sites that offer two-factor sign-in, where the item has no one-time code and no passkey saved.

#### How it works

The sites come from a list built into WM Pass, so nothing is looked up online.

See also [One-time codes](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-codes), [Passkeys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-passkeys).

<a id="action-health-check-duplicates"></a>

## Duplicate items

Lists logins saved more than once: the same site, the same username and the same password.

#### How it works

The Health page offers to merge each group. Choose the one that stays, and the others fold into it: their passwords move to its history, their extra fields come along, and the copies go to the trash.

See also [Used more than once](/guide/settings/health/#action-health-check-reused), [Trash](/guide/settings/trash/).
